newsitem.title: USA: Sun Microsystems stock tumbles after earnings report.
newsitem.headline: Sun Microsystems stock tumbles after earnings report.

text.p: Sun Microsystems Inc. stock took a beating Wednesday despite the computer maker's reporting a sharp rise in earnings that beat average forecasts on Wall Street.

Sun said late Tuesday that its profits jumped 45 percent in its fiscal first quarter to $123.4 million, or 63 cents a share, from $84.7 million, or 42 cents a share, in the 1995 quarter. It cited strong sales of its powerful computer workstations.
The profits were a shade above the average forecast of 61 cents a share as reported by First Call, which tracks earnings estimates, but investors started taking profits in after-hours trading.
Traders said the stock had run up ahead of the report, and that while Sun's numbers were strong, they were not as strong as some on Wall Street had come to expect.

The stock of the Mountain View, Calif.-based computer maker touched its all-time high of $70.25 on Tuesday before the earnings report and ended regular trading at $70. But it fell $4 in after-hours trading following the earnings report.
The freefall continued Wednesday, with the shares off $6.625 from Tuesday's closing price to $63.25 on Nasdaq.
"We've got to believe there's some profit-taking going on," Sun Chairman Scott McNealy told reporters in a conference call on Tuesday.
Some analysts saw the weakness in the stock as a buying opportunity.
Dean Witter analyst Jay Stevens said he raised his earnings estimates for Sun and reiterated a buy rating.
"They delivered a very fine quarter," Stevens said. But he added that the stock was down because some investors had expected even higher earnings.
